pool.text: Pedro de Valdivia officially founded Santiago del Nuevo Extremo on February 12.
A devastating earthquake struck Santiago, resulting in the death of over 600 people.
The First Government Junta was proclaimed in Santiago, marking independence.
The Spanish army progress was halted at the Battle of Maipú.
The first telegraph system connecting the capital to Valparaíso was inaugurated.
The Municipal Theater of Santiago was built by the French architect Brunet.
The National Stadium emerged in Santiago following shifts in popular entertainment venues.
The new Pudahuel International Airport was opened to the public.
The Torre Entel television tower with observation deck was completed.
The first phase of the Santiago Metro running beneath Alameda was opened.
A fire in the Torre Santa María killed 11 people in the city.
Santiago officially became part of the Union of Ibero American Capital Cities.
A powerful earthquake struck the city causing minimal casualties and damage.
The International Theater Festival known as Santiago a Mil takes place every January.
The Library of Santiago at Barrio Matucana was opened to the public.
Santiago was home to a total of 992000 vehicles within the city.
The master plan known as Transantiago was established for transportation.
The public transportation system combining core services with the subway was officially launched.
The Monticello Grand Casino opened in Mostazal situated south of Santiago.
The Costanera Center was completed, including housing, shopping, and entertainment.
